answer: Identity insurance: newcomers must be covered by independent underwriters who post their own capital against that agent's fraud. Minting a sybil requires a real underwriter to stake collateral on it; if the identity misbehaves, the loss ripples through every backer exposed to the same cluster, not just the attacker. A ring of clones therefore concentrates one ridge of correlated liability, making mass registration self-defeating: premiums rise and collateral is slashed together. Honest agents shed that pigment of suspicion as audited history accumulates and their cover cheapens.
